tests.name: Demographic Sensitivity Check for credit score assignment and borrower ranking
tests.objective: Detect whether changing only protected or comparison-group attributes changes credit score, rank, approval recommendation, or risk band beyond configured tolerance.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for credit-scoring application records: application_id, model_version, score, decision or rank, decision_threshold, timestamp, segment fields, and key credit-risk features.
Context fields for cohorting: protected or comparison-group attributes plus approved proxy candidates such as geography, employment type, education, device, and language.
Baseline or comparator: prior model version, holdout cohort, challenger scorecard, or customer historical monitoring window.
Protected or comparison-group attribute dictionary and approved proxy list.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for protected or comparison-group attributes plus approved proxy candidates such as geography, employment type, education, device, and language and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Create matched pairs and verify that non-target risk variables remain unchanged.
perturbation_strategy: Create one variant per controlled attribute value and one unchanged baseline record per evaluated case.
tests.technique: paired counterfactual consistency and demographic parity difference
method: Run or ingest baseline and paired-variant outcomes.
Calculate pair-level outcome flips and score shifts by controlled attribute.
Localize flips by segment, model version, and risk-band boundary.
primary_metrics: counterfactual_flip_rate: number of paired variants with changed outcome divided by valid paired variants. Direction: lower is better.
average_score_shift: mean absolute change in score or probability after only the controlled attribute changes. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: valid_pair_count: number of baseline/variant pairs that passed invariant checks. Direction: higher improves confidence.
boundary_flip_share: flips occurring within the configured decision-boundary band divided by all flips. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with policy-defined tolerance or configured MVP default; this is not a regulatory or industry threshold unless the policy itself provides the bound.
Use configured MVP default tolerance only as an internal decision aid; report confidence intervals when sample size allows.
failure_criteria: If counterfactual flip rate or score shift exceeds the configured tolerance: flag protected-attribute sensitivity for review
If valid paired evidence is below the minimum group size: mark the test insufficient evidence rather than treating disparity as stable
recommendation_logic: If paired flips exceed tolerance: inspect drivers for proxy leakage, constrain or retrain affected features, and rerun the paired evaluation
If sample size is insufficient: collect representative evidence before drawing population-level fairness conclusions

method: Rank proxy candidates by conditional association with outcomes.
Run paired proxy substitutions for high-risk proxies.

primary_metrics: proxy_influence_rate: proxy substitutions that materially change the outcome divided by valid proxy variants. Direction: lower is better.
conditional_disparity_gap: largest outcome-rate difference across proxy values inside comparable risk strata. Direction: lower is better.

tests.name: Demographic Sensitivity Check for fraud scoring, alerting, and suspicious behavior detection
tests.objective: Detect whether changing only protected or comparison-group attributes changes fraud score, alert decision, case priority, or block/escalate action beyond configured tolerance.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for fraud transaction or account-behavior records: transaction_id or account_id, model_version, fraud_score, alert_threshold, alert decision, timestamp, attack or merchant segment, and device/network indicators.
Context fields for cohorting: merchant category, device age, transaction channel, geography, customer tenure, fraud scenario, and account-risk cohort.
Baseline or comparator: clean transaction cohort, previous model version, analyst-reviewed labels, or synthetic fraud robustness reference.
Protected or comparison-group attribute dictionary and approved proxy list.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for merchant category, device age, transaction channel, geography, customer tenure, fraud scenario, and account-risk cohort and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Create matched pairs and verify that non-target risk variables remain unchanged.
perturbation_strategy: Create one variant per controlled attribute value and one unchanged baseline record per evaluated case.
tests.technique: paired counterfactual consistency and demographic parity difference
method: Run or ingest baseline and paired-variant outcomes.
Calculate pair-level outcome flips and score shifts by controlled attribute.
Localize flips by segment, model version, and risk-band boundary.
primary_metrics: counterfactual_flip_rate: number of paired variants with changed outcome divided by valid paired variants. Direction: lower is better.
average_score_shift: mean absolute change in score or probability after only the controlled attribute changes. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: valid_pair_count: number of baseline/variant pairs that passed invariant checks. Direction: higher improves confidence.
boundary_flip_share: flips occurring within the configured decision-boundary band divided by all flips. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with policy-defined tolerance or configured MVP default; this is not a regulatory or industry threshold unless the policy itself provides the bound.
Use configured MVP default tolerance only as an internal decision aid; report confidence intervals when sample size allows.
failure_criteria: If counterfactual flip rate or score shift exceeds the configured tolerance: flag protected-attribute sensitivity for review
If valid paired evidence is below the minimum group size: mark the test insufficient evidence rather than treating disparity as stable
recommendation_logic: If paired flips exceed tolerance: inspect drivers for proxy leakage, constrain or retrain affected features, and rerun the paired evaluation
If sample size is insufficient: collect representative evidence before drawing population-level fairness conclusions

tests.name: Proxy Attribute Detection for fraud scoring, alerting, and suspicious behavior detection
tests.objective: Detect whether approved proxy candidates disproportionately influence fraud score, alert decision, case priority, or block/escalate action after legitimate risk variables are held constant.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for fraud transaction or account-behavior records: transaction_id or account_id, model_version, fraud_score, alert_threshold, alert decision, timestamp, attack or merchant segment, and device/network indicators.
Context fields for cohorting: merchant category, device age, transaction channel, geography, customer tenure, fraud scenario, and account-risk cohort.
Baseline or comparator: clean transaction cohort, previous model version, analyst-reviewed labels, or synthetic fraud robustness reference.
Proxy-candidate dictionary, feature lineage, and business justification for each proxy field.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for merchant category, device age, transaction channel, geography, customer tenure, fraud scenario, and account-risk cohort and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Normalize proxy values and stratify by comparable risk bands before measuring proxy effects.
perturbation_strategy: Vary one proxy candidate at a time inside documented business-plausible ranges while holding protected attributes and core risk variables invariant.
tests.technique: proxy sensitivity analysis with conditional outcome comparison
method: Rank proxy candidates by conditional association with outcomes.
Run paired proxy substitutions for high-risk proxies.
Compare proxy-driven score shifts against policy tolerance and segment concentration.
primary_metrics: proxy_influence_rate: proxy substitutions that materially change the outcome divided by valid proxy variants. Direction: lower is better.
conditional_disparity_gap: largest outcome-rate difference across proxy values inside comparable risk strata. Direction: lower is better.

recommendation_logic: If unjustified proxy influence is detected: remove, transform, constrain, or document the proxy and rerun sensitivity tests
If coverage is sparse: improve feature lineage and data capture before using the result for model changes

tests.technique: multi-factor paired counterfactual fairness evaluation with uncertainty reporting
method: Run paired comparisons across all scenario families.
Estimate worst-case and average flip rates with bootstrap confidence intervals where sample size permits.
Assess interaction effects between protected attributes, proxies, and boundary proximity.
Produce severity-weighted fairness findings by cohort.

recommendation_logic: If paired flips exceed tolerance: inspect drivers for proxy leakage, constrain or retrain affected features, and rerun the paired evaluation
If sample size is insufficient: collect representative evidence before drawing population-level fairness conclusions

tests.name: Demographic Sensitivity Check for underwriting recommendations, policy checks, and decision rationale
tests.objective: Detect whether changing only protected or comparison-group attributes changes underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy exception, stipulation, or manual-review decision beyond configured tolerance.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for underwriting recommendation and policy-check records: application_id, model_version, underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy checks, threshold or cutoff, timestamp, segment fields, and reviewer outcome where available.
Context fields for cohorting: product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment.
Baseline or comparator: policy rule baseline, senior-underwriter review sample, previous model version, or customer historical underwriting cohort.
Protected or comparison-group attribute dictionary and approved proxy list.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Create matched pairs and verify that non-target risk variables remain unchanged.
perturbation_strategy: Create one variant per controlled attribute value and one unchanged baseline record per evaluated case.
tests.technique: paired counterfactual consistency and demographic parity difference
method: Run or ingest baseline and paired-variant outcomes.
Calculate pair-level outcome flips and score shifts by controlled attribute.
Localize flips by segment, model version, and risk-band boundary.
primary_metrics: counterfactual_flip_rate: number of paired variants with changed outcome divided by valid paired variants. Direction: lower is better.
average_score_shift: mean absolute change in score or probability after only the controlled attribute changes. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: valid_pair_count: number of baseline/variant pairs that passed invariant checks. Direction: higher improves confidence.
boundary_flip_share: flips occurring within the configured decision-boundary band divided by all flips. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with policy-defined tolerance or configured MVP default; this is not a regulatory or industry threshold unless the policy itself provides the bound.
Use configured MVP default tolerance only as an internal decision aid; report confidence intervals when sample size allows.
failure_criteria: If counterfactual flip rate or score shift exceeds the configured tolerance: flag protected-attribute sensitivity for review
If valid paired evidence is below the minimum group size: mark the test insufficient evidence rather than treating disparity as stable
recommendation_logic: If paired flips exceed tolerance: inspect drivers for proxy leakage, constrain or retrain affected features, and rerun the paired evaluation
If sample size is insufficient: collect representative evidence before drawing population-level fairness conclusions

tests.name: Proxy Attribute Detection for underwriting recommendations, policy checks, and decision rationale
tests.objective: Detect whether approved proxy candidates disproportionately influence underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy exception, stipulation, or manual-review decision after legitimate risk variables are held constant.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for underwriting recommendation and policy-check records: application_id, model_version, underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy checks, threshold or cutoff, timestamp, segment fields, and reviewer outcome where available.
Context fields for cohorting: product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment.
Baseline or comparator: policy rule baseline, senior-underwriter review sample, previous model version, or customer historical underwriting cohort.
Proxy-candidate dictionary, feature lineage, and business justification for each proxy field.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Normalize proxy values and stratify by comparable risk bands before measuring proxy effects.
perturbation_strategy: Vary one proxy candidate at a time inside documented business-plausible ranges while holding protected attributes and core risk variables invariant.
tests.technique: proxy sensitivity analysis with conditional outcome comparison
method: Rank proxy candidates by conditional association with outcomes.
Run paired proxy substitutions for high-risk proxies.
Compare proxy-driven score shifts against policy tolerance and segment concentration.
primary_metrics: proxy_influence_rate: proxy substitutions that materially change the outcome divided by valid proxy variants. Direction: lower is better.
conditional_disparity_gap: largest outcome-rate difference across proxy values inside comparable risk strata. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: proxy_coverage: share of records with populated proxy candidates. Direction: higher improves confidence.
segment_contribution: share of total disparity attributable to each proxy/segment pair. Direction: lower concentration is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with policy-defined tolerance or configured MVP default; this is not a regulatory or industry threshold unless the policy itself provides the bound.
Compare against documented feature-use policy and internal historical proxy-sensitivity results.
failure_criteria: If a proxy has material outcome influence without documented business justification: flag proxy-bias risk
If proxy coverage is too sparse for a stable estimate: mark affected proxy findings not assessable
recommendation_logic: If unjustified proxy influence is detected: remove, transform, constrain, or document the proxy and rerun sensitivity tests
If coverage is sparse: improve feature lineage and data capture before using the result for model changes

tests.name: Language Bias Detection for underwriting recommendations, policy checks, and decision rationale
tests.objective: Detect whether tone, language, formality, or borrower wording changes underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy exception, stipulation, or manual-review decision when financial facts are unchanged.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for underwriting recommendation and policy-check records: application_id, model_version, underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy checks, threshold or cutoff, timestamp, segment fields, and reviewer outcome where available.
Context fields for cohorting: product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment.
Baseline or comparator: policy rule baseline, senior-underwriter review sample, previous model version, or customer historical underwriting cohort.
Original text fields, normalized semantic labels, language/formality labels, and unchanged structured risk features.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Separate semantic content from style attributes and reject variants that change financial facts.
perturbation_strategy: Generate language, tone, spelling, or formality variants that preserve borrower facts, requested product, and policy context.
method: Create semantic-preserving wording variants.
Compare model outputs between original and variants.
Group failures by language, style, segment, and model version.
primary_metrics: language_style_flip_rate: wording variants that change the outcome divided by valid wording variants. Direction: lower is better.
semantic_consistency_score: one minus the share of semantically equivalent variants with materially different outcomes. Direction: higher is better.
secondary_metrics: variant_rejection_rate: generated variants rejected for changing facts divided by proposed variants. Direction: lower indicates cleaner perturbations.
language_group_failure_count: number of failures per language or style cohort. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with a customer-internal historical baseline or challenger baseline that used the same evidence contract, model version scope, time window definition, and scoring implementation.
Compare with previous model or template baseline evaluated on the same semantic-preserving variant set.
failure_criteria: If semantically equivalent variants produce inconsistent outcomes beyond tolerance: flag language-bias risk
If variants cannot be verified as fact-preserving: mark affected cases not assessable
recommendation_logic: If language/style inconsistency is material: add style-invariant training or constraints and retest with verified semantic pairs
If variant quality is weak: tighten variant review before interpreting model sensitivity

tests.name: Counterfactual Fairness Evaluation for underwriting recommendations, policy checks, and decision rationale
tests.objective: Evaluate protected-attribute, proxy, and language sensitivity together to identify worst-case fairness failures in underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy exception, stipulation, or manual-review decision.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for underwriting recommendation and policy-check records: application_id, model_version, underwriting recommendation, risk tier, policy checks, threshold or cutoff, timestamp, segment fields, and reviewer outcome where available.
Context fields for cohorting: product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment.
Baseline or comparator: policy rule baseline, senior-underwriter review sample, previous model version, or customer historical underwriting cohort.
Joined evidence containing baseline records, controlled variants, proxy dictionary, segment labels, decision thresholds, and model version.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.
Deduplicate records by stable identifier and keep an audit trail of removed duplicates, invalid rows, and not-assessable cases.

Construct analysis cohorts for product, collateral type, employment type, geography, channel, exception type, reviewer cohort, and borrower segment and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Build a reproducible paired evaluation matrix and compute uncertainty only for cohorts meeting minimum size.
perturbation_strategy: Combine protected-attribute, proxy, and language/style variants under a fixed scenario matrix while preserving legitimate risk variables and business plausibility.
tests.technique: multi-factor paired counterfactual fairness evaluation with uncertainty reporting
method: Run paired comparisons across all scenario families.
Estimate worst-case and average flip rates with bootstrap confidence intervals where sample size permits.
Assess interaction effects between protected attributes, proxies, and boundary proximity.
Produce severity-weighted fairness findings by cohort.
primary_metrics: worst_case_counterfactual_flip_rate: maximum valid flip rate across scenario families and cohorts. Direction: lower is better.
severity_weighted_bias_score: weighted failure score combining flip rate, score shift, boundary proximity, and affected-record count. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: bootstrap_interval_width: confidence interval width for key disparity estimates. Direction: lower improves certainty.
interaction_failure_count: number of failures caused only by combined protected/proxy/style perturbations. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare only with illustrative synthetic reference distributions until comparable evaluator versions, evidence contracts, cohort definitions, anonymization, jurisdiction/product segmentation, time windows, minimum cohort size, and uncertainty reporting exist.
Illustrative synthetic reference distributions may contextualize severity, but not as verified Lendingtech industry percentiles.
failure_criteria: If worst-case or severity-weighted bias exceeds configured tolerance: flag strong fairness failure
If confidence intervals are too wide: label population inference uncertain even if directional risk is visible
recommendation_logic: If strong fairness failure is confirmed: prioritize affected cohorts, adjust feature constraints or model training, document residual risk, and rerun the full scenario matrix
If uncertainty is high: expand labeled evidence before using the finding as a benchmarkable result

inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for OCR document-extraction records: document_id, document_type, model_version, extracted fields, field-level confidence, timestamp, document-quality metadata, and ground-truth or reviewed values when available.
Context fields for cohorting: document type, language, image quality, scan channel, field type, template family, and downstream workflow.
Baseline or comparator: reviewed extraction sample, template-specific holdout set, previous OCR model, or clean document cohort.
Protected or comparison-group attribute dictionary and approved proxy list.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.

Construct analysis cohorts for document type, language, image quality, scan channel, field type, template family, and downstream workflow and verify minimum group sizes before interpreting stable population differences.
Create matched pairs and verify that non-target risk variables remain unchanged.
perturbation_strategy: Create one variant per controlled attribute value and one unchanged baseline record per evaluated case.
tests.technique: paired counterfactual consistency and demographic parity difference
method: Run or ingest baseline and paired-variant outcomes.
Calculate pair-level outcome flips and score shifts by controlled attribute.
Localize flips by segment, model version, and risk-band boundary.
primary_metrics: counterfactual_flip_rate: number of paired variants with changed outcome divided by valid paired variants. Direction: lower is better.
average_score_shift: mean absolute change in score or probability after only the controlled attribute changes. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: valid_pair_count: number of baseline/variant pairs that passed invariant checks. Direction: higher improves confidence.
boundary_flip_share: flips occurring within the configured decision-boundary band divided by all flips. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with policy-defined tolerance or configured MVP default; this is not a regulatory or industry threshold unless the policy itself provides the bound.
Use configured MVP default tolerance only as an internal decision aid; report confidence intervals when sample size allows.
failure_criteria: If counterfactual flip rate or score shift exceeds the configured tolerance: flag protected-attribute sensitivity for review
If valid paired evidence is below the minimum group size: mark the test insufficient evidence rather than treating disparity as stable
recommendation_logic: If paired flips exceed tolerance: inspect drivers for proxy leakage, constrain or retrain affected features, and rerun the paired evaluation
If sample size is insufficient: collect representative evidence before drawing population-level fairness conclusions

tests.name: Proxy Attribute Detection for extracted document fields used in identity, income, and underwriting workflows
tests.objective: Detect whether approved proxy candidates disproportionately influence extracted field value, field confidence, document-level confidence, validation decision, or manual-review flag after legitimate risk variables are held constant.
inputs_required: Primary diagnostic evidence for OCR document-extraction records: document_id, document_type, model_version, extracted fields, field-level confidence, timestamp, document-quality metadata, and ground-truth or reviewed values when available.

Proxy-candidate dictionary, feature lineage, and business justification for each proxy field.
preprocessing_steps: Validate the evidence schema, required identifiers, model version, timestamps, and outcome fields before scoring.
Coerce numeric scores, thresholds, probabilities, dates, and confidence values without imputing values that are evidence for the tested failure.

Compare proxy-driven score shifts against policy tolerance and segment concentration.

If coverage is sparse: improve feature lineage and data capture before using the result for model changes

primary_metrics: counterfactual_flip_rate: number of paired variants with changed outcome divided by valid paired variants. Direction: lower is better.
average_score_shift: mean absolute change in score or probability after only the controlled attribute changes. Direction: lower is better.
secondary_metrics: valid_pair_count: number of baseline/variant pairs that passed invariant checks. Direction: higher improves confidence.
boundary_flip_share: flips occurring within the configured decision-boundary band divided by all flips. Direction: lower is better.
benchmark_interpretation: Compare with policy-defined tolerance or configured MVP default; this is not a regulatory or industry threshold unless the policy itself provides the bound.
Use configured MVP default tolerance only as an internal decision aid; report confidence intervals when sample size allows.
failure_criteria: If counterfactual flip rate or score shift exceeds the configured tolerance: flag protected-attribute sensitivity for review

recommendation_logic: If paired flips exceed tolerance: inspect drivers for proxy leakage, constrain or retrain affected features, and rerun the paired evaluation
If sample size is insufficient: collect representative evidence before drawing population-level fairness conclusions
